summary: Arabic has singular, dual and plural; sound plurals (-ūn/-īn, -āt) and broken plurals. Most vegetables are collective nouns: جَزَر (carrots, as a kind); one piece is the unit noun جَزَرَة, counted pieces take -āt: جَزَرَات.

askYourself: Do I mean the vegetable in general (→ collective) or counted pieces (→ unit noun, plural -āt)?

traps: The sound feminine plural has -i (not -a) in the accusative: الْجَزَرَاتِ.
Non-human plurals take feminine singular agreement.
